title: Metric lineage and trace-mapping sprint plan
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an actionable sprint plan to produce a first-pass metric-lineage registry, map critical trace spans to dashboard widgets, and define acceptance criteria for metric correctness. Goal: reduce investigation time for token-latency incidents by 30% through clear provenance and a small trace-playlist for oncall.

Scope / non-goals:
- In-scope: top 40 operational metrics (latency, error rate, kv-cache warmth, queue depth, tail-percentiles), their producers, transformations, consumers (dashboards/alerts), and trace span anchors.
- Out-of-scope: full company-wide metric catalog (follow-up). No changes to instrumentation libraries in this sprint unless low-risk.

High-level deliverables (end of sprint):
1) Metric-lineage CSV + short doc for each metric describing origin, transformation (aggregation/windowing), owner, and consumer widgets.
2) Trace-to-widget mapping: for each dashboard widget, a canonical span id or span pattern + sample trace query.
3) Dashboard index (compact): widget owner, query, and SLI mapping.
4) Draft sampling/retention tiers (hot/warm/cold) for traces tied to metric criticality.
5) Oncall trace-playlist (5 curated traces + short playbook).

Definitions / shorthand used here:
- Producer: service/component that emits the raw metric or event (e.g., router, runtime-gpu, kv-prefetcher).
- Transform: a pipeline step where metrics are aggregated, normalized, or derived (e.g., counter -> per-second rate with 1m window).
- Anchor span: the trace span(s) that most directly correlate to metric observations (session-create, model-forward, kv-lookup).

Metric lineage model (template to collect):
- metric_name: e.g., inference.time_to_first_token_ms
- level: agent|service|platform
- producer: service/service-subcomponent
- event_emitted: yes/no (event vs metric)
- transform: SQL/query or prom rule applied
- consumer_dashboards: list of widgets
- alerting_policy: alert id or none
- owner: primary

Example (filled):
- metric_name: inference.time_to_first_token_ms
- level: service
- producer: runtime-proxy
- event_emitted: no (histogram)
- transform: 95th percentile over 1m rolling window (prom: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(...)))
- consumer_dashboards: ops/token-latency-overview#panel-3
- alerting_policy: ALERT-OBS-102
- owner: Miguel Torres

Trace mapping approach:
- For each producer, identify the minimal set of spans that explain metric variance. Map to span names and key attributes (e.g., model.name, tenant.id, prompt_length).
- Provide one example trace search query (X-Ray, Jaeger or our trace-store) and one stored example trace id for replay.
- Add a short note on sampling: if the producer is high-volume, note sample rate and rationale.

Trace-to-widget mapping examples:
- Widget: token-latency: p95 by model family
  Anchor spans: model.forward, runtime-queue.wait
  Trace query: service=runtime and span in (model.forward, runtime-queue.wait) | tags(model.family) | sort by duration desc
  Owner: Priya Kapoor

- Widget: kv-cache-hit-rate (tenant-level)
  Anchor spans: kv.lookup
  Trace query: service=kv-cache and span=kv.lookup and tag(tenant_id) | group by tenant_id | sample 100
  Owner: Liam O'Neill

Sprint backlog (3-week chunk) - condensed stories:
1) Build metric-lineage CSV template and populate top 20 metrics (3d) - Owner: Ava (est: 3d) - JIRA: OBS-4823
2) Identify anchor spans for top 20 metrics and store queries (4d) - Owner: Priya (est: 4d)
3) Dashboard index: compile widgets -> owners -> SLI mapping (2d) - Owner: Miguel (est: 2d)
4) Implement trace sampling tier proposal (hot/warm/cold) and write rollout note (2d) - Owner: Ava + SRE (est: 2d)
5) Oncall trace-playlist + mini-runbook for token-latency incidents (2d) - Owner: Miguel (est: 2d)
6) Integrate a small automation to attach lineage metadata to alert pages (proof-of-concept) (4d) - Owner: Priya (est: 4d)
7) Stakeholder review + doc clean-up (1d) - Owner: Ava (est: 1d)

Acceptance criteria (for each delivered artifact):
- Metric-lineage CSV: every row has producer, transform, consumer, owner, and at least one linked_artifact (dashboard or alert).
- Trace mapping: each widget linked in CSV has at least one anchor span and a working trace query that reproduces a slow sample within the last 30 days.
- Dashboard index: every high-sev alert references the widget row in CSV.
- Sampling tiers: a documented guideline that allows ops to increase sampling for a metric bucket within 15 minutes.
- Automation POC: when viewing an alert page, there is a link to the metric-lineage row.

Sampling / retention tiers (proposal):
- Hot (critical metrics, top 10): full trace retention 7d, sample rate 1/10 for traces with duration > p90.
- Warm (mid criticality): 3d retention, 1/100 sampling, sample all error traces.
- Cold (lower criticality experiments): 24h retention, 1/1000 sampling, error-only retention.
Notes: correlate retention to SLI budget and query cost; refine after cost simulation.

Dashboard index (compact format to implement):
- slug: ops/token-latency-overview; panels: p1(p50), p2(p95 by model), p3(tf breakdown); primary_owner: Miguel; sla_mapping: SLI-TTF-95 -> Alert-102

Trace-playlist (starter):
- TP-1: model-forward-degradation: span sequence model.forward -> runtime-queue.wait -> network-call. Repro: trace id stored in OBS-TP-1.
- TP-2: kv-cache-eviction-blip: trace showing high-prefetch and kv.miss bursts. Repro: OBS-TP-2.
- TP-3: cold-start-slow-path: cold model load sequence.
- Note: store one canonical trace per playlist item in the trace-store with searchable tags.

Open questions / risks (to surface in review):
- Cost sensitivity: our proposed hot retention (7d) may double trace-store costs if not limited by duration thresholds. Need SRE cost simulation (action: SRE to estimate).
- Ownership gaps: several infra-generated metrics lack clear single owners; propose namespacing and follow-up owner-assignment ticket.
- Instrumentation changes: some metrics (derived from logs) are fragile; might need library changes that exceed sprint scope.

Next steps / immediate asks:
- Review and sanity-check the top-20 metric list (owners listed inline). Please add missing owners by EOD Friday.
- SRE: quick cost estimate for the proposed retention tiers by Tuesday.
- Dashboard product: confirm that attaching lineage links to alert pages is acceptable UX.

Notes-to-self (working):
- Keep the lineage CSV minimal for quick wins; avoid over-normalizing fields in first pass.
- When mapping spans, prefer context-rich attributes (model.name, tenant.id) to allow grouping in dashboards.
- Save sample traces for 90 days in a cheap bucket for debugging cross-sprint regressions.

Appendix: quick checklist for reviewers:
- [ ] Producers listed for all top-20 metrics
- [ ] At least one anchor span per widget
- [ ] Trace queries validated and reproducing a slow trace from last 30 days
- [ ] Sampling tiers sanity-checked by SRE
- [ ] Owners assigned for leftover metrics

---
Revision log (keeps short):
- 2025-11-10: initial draft (Ava)
- 2025-12-05: added sampling tier proposal and sprint backlog (Priya)
- 2026-02-14: updated acceptance criteria and trace-playlist (Miguel)

End of doc.
